# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is a tidyverse-based re-implementation of the
[NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/),
originally published as a static HTML handbook with worked examples in
[Dataplot](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/).

Each chapter follows the structure of the original handbook, but the worked
examples are reproduced using R and the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/)
family of packages (`dplyr`, `tidyr`, `ggplot2`, `purrr`, `broom`, and related
extensions). Original datasets are retained for reference and validation.

The source content for this migration lives in `handbook/` at the root of
this repository.

## Why this edition exists

I first became aware of the e-Handbook in the early 2000s, while working in
optical metrology (reflectometry, ellipsometry, and scatterometry) for a
semiconductor capital equipment company — the content was directly
applicable to my role as an application scientist. I have continued to use
it throughout my career, including outside the semiconductor industry, and
eventually as a primary text for a graduate-level applied statistics course
I have taught for almost a decade.

The content and examples in the e-Handbook are excellent and meet its
stated objective to "help scientists and engineers incorporate statistical
methods into their work as efficiently as possible." While minor corrections
have been made over the years, the last major update is reported as April
2012, and the layout — a 1990s-era HTML frameset — is less than ideal for
modern use. An additional challenge to using the e-Handbook as a primary
course text has been the infrequent, but always poorly timed, shutdowns of
the U.S. government, which take the website offline along with it. (I have
made a `handbook.zip` snapshot available to students in the past, but this
is far from an ideal substitute for a working site.)

This edition exists to address both problems: a modern, searchable book
format, and a local, version-controlled copy that doesn't depend on any
single website staying up. See the "Methodology" appendix for how it was
produced, and "About the Editor" for more on who put it together.
